description: turbopack-core: ModuleGraphLayer::reachable_subgraph_hashes, a keyed map from each module of a layer to a 128-bit hash of what a traversal from it can see (the module, whether it is an entry, and every edge reachable from it in order, with its RefData and whether binding usage marks it unused; one pass over the strongly connected components in reverse topological order). next-api's per-endpoint queries over a whole-app layer (next/dynamic imports, server actions, client references) read their entry's hash keyed and the layer untracked, so after a new import only the endpoints that reach the changed subgraph traverse again. Test: with entries a and b, a new import under b leaves a's hash and traversal alone; a new import under a, and an edge under a becoming traced, run a's traversal again with the new result; the same test fails with the layer read tracked. Not taken: with new imports a warm build's run-turbopack is longer on 24 CPUs (9.4s against 10.0s after one) and no shorter on 8 or 192 (cache-drift.md)
